ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, enforced by FINTRAC. Quebec: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 32.2–32.5 (register of individuals with significant control) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, as amended (mandatory REQ beneficial-ownership declarations). Federal: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 146.1–146.6, if a federal Business Corporation is instead selected.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO information filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec and FINTRAC is not available through unrestricted public searches; access is restricted to REQ, federal and provincial tax authorities, FINTRAC, and domestic law enforcement/prosecutorial agencies on lawful request)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), Quebec, Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (domestic issuance; apostilles for Canadian public documents are issued by designated federal and provincial authorities and do not require consular legalization for use in other Hague member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Legal Existence of the non-resident parent or shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the parent entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the parent registry's competent authority if the parent is located in a Hague Apostille Convention member state; otherwise Consular Legalization through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant Canadian consular or diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Copy of Passport and Proof of Residential Address of each director, officer, and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the origin country's competent authority, followed by certified English or French translation for REQ filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorizing the Quebec incorporation agent and notary to execute Articles of Incorporation, UBO declarations, and REQ filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarized execution by the corporate legal representative of the parent entity or by the individual UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-origin powers of attorney; domestic Quebec powers of attorney may be notarized before a Quebec notary under the Act respecting notaries, CQLR c N-3

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Confirmation Letter and Source-of-Funds Reference for the incorporation trust account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed deposit-taking institution maintaining the corporate bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or bank-correspondent SWIFT verification where required by the Quebec notary's source-of-funds diligence; certified translation into French or English if issued in a non-official language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and executive officers against: (a) FINTRAC-validated global PEP databases; (b) the Government of Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and sanctions listed under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) administered by Global Affairs Canada; (c) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List as incorporated under the United Nations Act and the Criminal Code; (d) the U.S. OFAC SDN List and the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List as market-standard cross-checks for USD-denominated payment rails; and (e) RCMP and Criminal Intelligence Service Canada watchlists. Standard financial services guidance under the PCMLTFA applies: the MMORPG software publishing model is assessed as a low-risk standard category without statutory licensing, yet 25% UBO threshold verification, meaningful source-of-funds documentation, and a written corporate AML policy remain mandatory before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises Online Name Search and Name Reservation Portal (https://registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, and the Quebec Business Corporations Act, s. 12, the legal name of a Quebec business corporation must be in French and a French version is compulsory for registration. A secondary version in another language, such as English or Chinese, is permissible but the French form governs the legal identity. Transliterations must use Latin script with a statutorily acceptable phonetic rendering; names must not be scandalous, misleading, or contravene public order. REQ performs a full corpora language database search across Quebec provincial and Canadian federal corporate records before reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ name rejection, the applicant may: (i) file a new name-search reservation within 90 days of the rejection notice with only the standard analysis-report tariff payable; (ii) submit a written reconsideration request to the REQ Name Analysis Service within 30 days of the rejection, attaching any registered trademark evidence or distinguishable brand-usage documentation for a reason-based override; and (iii) if reconsideration is denied, file a judicial appeal before the Court of Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, s. 44, within 30 days of the reconsideration denial, where the court may order REQ to register the name upon proof of no regulatory confusion and absence of statutory misrepresentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for an ISIC 5820 software publisher: a virtual office is acceptable if it comprises a physical street address in Quebec, is not a mail-only drop, has attended personnel during ordinary business hours, and guarantees service of process through a registered agent under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; pure post-office-box addresses and unattended virtual addresses are prohibited.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-risk band, approximately 5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first fiscal year; REQ and the Canada Revenue Agency conduct no routine on-site inspections for the unlicensed, low-risk MMORPG publishing industry. An unannounced visit would realistically be triggered only by GST/QST audit indicators, UBO declaration inconsistencies, or third-party complaints alleging a sham mailbox entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), RLRQ c S-31.1, ss. 7-20 (constitution by articles of incorporation), s. 25 (registered office), ss. 34-38 (directors), s. 115 (by-laws); registry governed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises), RLRQ c P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Enterprise Register of Quebec) — CliquezAffaires online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; authorized capital may consist of one or more shares with or without par value. No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated at incorporation. Consideration for issued shares may be money, property, or past services; a solvency test must be met before any share repurchase.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Corporation was duly constituted under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the subscriber has executed the Articles of Incorporation; RESOLVED that the subscription for 100 common shares without par value is accepted and that share certificates be issued; RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at 1250 René-Lévesque Boulevard West, Montréal, Québec H3B 4W8, Canada; RESOLVED that the by-law respecting the conduct of the Corporation's affairs, tabled at this meeting, is adopted; RESOLVED that A— is appointed President, B— Secretary, and C— Treasurer, to serve until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to open banking accounts and carry out all acts necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CliquezAffaires online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the Central Registry of Enterprise Names to confirm that the proposed English or French corporate name is distinct and not confusing with existing trademarks or legal persons. File the name reservation request electronically, pay the prescribed fee (CAD 38), and obtain the reservation certificate. Use the reserved word within its validity period (up to 90 days) or renew.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Proposed corporate name with legal element (Inc., Corp., or the French equivalent)
Incorporator's identification (name, address, date and place of birth for natural persons)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for distinctiveness issues, the Registraire issues a written refusal notice identifying the conflicting name. File a revised reservation with a new distinctive element; alternatively, submit a written justification with supporting trademark evidence within the specified contestation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator (shareholder) and, if applicable, legal counsel; filing by electronic signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts de constitution in French or English (French is recommended for full legal effect under the Charter of the French Language). The articles must state the corporate name, authorized share structure, restrictions (if any), number and residency requirements of directors, and the registered office address. The incorporator signs the articles; electronic signature is accepted through CliquezAffaires. The incorporator is not personally liable for the corporation's obligations.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
Name reservation certificate (if obtained)
Mandate or power of attorney for signing counsel (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire queries the articles for omissions or conflicting provisions, amend and resubmit the corrected instrument; structural defects in the share or director clauses may be cured by a special resolution of shareholders after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Issuance of Certificate of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CliquezAffaires secure transaction service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed articles electronically through CliquezAffaires, pay the constitution fee (CAD 171, plus registration fee CAD 4.13), and receive the Certificat de constitution and the enterprise registration number (NEQ) electronically. The corporation acquires legal personality on the date of the certificate. The registered office address and the first directors are those declared in the articles.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation certificate
Signed Articles of Incorporation in final form
Payment instrument (credit card or pre-authorized debit)
Consent to act as director of each named director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is refused for formal defects, the Registraire issues an avis de refus; correct the defects and refile within the applicable term, or, if the refusal rests on legal grounds, request an administrative review before the Directeur général du Registraire or institute a recourse in the Superior Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting — By-Laws, Share Subscriptions, Registered Office and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation (internal governance act; minutes kept in the corporate records book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting after the certificate of constitution. Adopt the general by-law No. 1 (Règlement administratif), accept share subscriptions, issue share certificates, confirm the registered office address, appoint officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer) and approve the corporate seal and banking resolutions. Minutes must be signed and preserved at the registered office, with a French version prepared if minutes are kept in English.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution (Certificat de constitution)
Draft by-law No. 1
Subscriptions and share certificate ledger
Register of directors (names, residential addresses, consent forms)
First board meeting minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Director consent irregularities are cured by obtaining signed consents to act; if an appointed officer resigns or is unavailable, the board adopts a supplementary resolution filling the vacancy and updates the register of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Statutory Registrations (Revenu Québec and CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (GST/QST and corporate income tax); Canada Revenue Agency (payroll and GST through Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new corporation with Revenu Québec for Quebec corporate income tax and QST using the NEQ; obtain the GST number through the CRA-Revenu Québec integrated registration when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. If employees are hired, open a payroll deduction account with Revenu Québec and a CRA payroll program account. Declare each place of business (établissement) in the Registre des entreprises. Choose a fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31) for the corporate income tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and NEQ
Registered office address and place of business details
Directors' names, addresses, and countries of residence
Business activity description (NAICS 511210)
Estimated annual taxable supplies and intended fiscal year-end
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrations are partially processed, Revenu Québec sends a request for information; complete the missing schedules within 30 days. Late GST/QST registration penalties may be reduced under the reasonable-cause relief provisions administered by the CRA and Revenu Québec.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — software publishing (NAICS 511210) is an unregulated non-manufacturing activity in Quebec; no industrial licensing board authorization is required. Municipal zoning and building permits apply only to the physical office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required for MMORPG publishing. The mandatory registry is the business registration (immatriculation) with the Registraire des entreprises (NEQ), and, when operating, the tax accounts opened with Revenu Québec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software publishing is not listed in the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (RLRQ c Q-2, r. 23); no full EIA or attestation of authorization is required for this activity under the Environmental Quality Act (RLRQ c Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated industrial point-source discharges, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste thresholds apply to server/office operations. The corporation must nonetheless comply with municipal solid-waste and recycling by-laws (paper, packaging, and e-waste) and with the Regulation respecting the recovery of electrical and electronic equipment when disposing of IT hardware. Data-center colocation contracts must include the operator's environmental compliance warranties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain an attestation de sécurité incendie from the municipal fire prevention service (e.g., Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal) for the leased office premises and comply with the Building Act (RLRQ c B-1.1), the Quebec Construction Code, and the Fire Safety Code. Occupational health: register with the CNESST, adopt a workplace prevention program (Plan d'action SST) under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (RLRQ c S-2.1), provide ergonomic workstations for software developers, and post workplace notices; no structural load inspection is required for standard office occupancy, but a change of use or fit-up triggers a municipal permit review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada), portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html); and Revenu Quebec, portal: Mon dossier d'entreprise / CLIC (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/). For a Quebec-resident corporation, Revenu Quebec administers the federal GST, the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), and Quebec corporation income tax under the Canada-Quebec Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement, while the CRA retains federal income tax, payroll, and international audit jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) under the Canada Business Corporations Act via Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre (federal fee CAD 200) or under the Quebec Business Corporations Act via the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ); obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and, for Quebec, the 10-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Step 2: Register for the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) and tax accounts (GST/HST account, corporate income tax, payroll) through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) service; the BN serves as the statutory tax identification number for all federal taxes. Step 3: Register all Quebec tax accounts with Revenu Quebec, including the QST/TVQ account, provincial corporation tax account, and employer source-deduction accounts; obtain the 16-character QST registration number (prefix TQ) linked to the NEQ. Step 4: Activate CRA My Business Account and Revenu Quebec CLIC digital credentials for mandatory electronic filing (GST/HST via Netfile, Quebec CO-17 corporation tax return, and provincial remittances). Step 5: No further TIN procurement is required: the corporation is Canadian-resident, non-resident ownership is permitted without restriction, and no minimum paid-up capital is legally required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid entity election exists under Canadian income tax law; a Business Corporation is compulsorily taxed as a separate person at entity level under Part I of the Income Tax Act (RSC 1985, c.1) and the Quebec Taxation Act (RLRQ c. I-3) on worldwide income with foreign tax credits. Available elections relevant to a Quebec MMORPG publisher: (i) Excise Tax Act (ETA) subsection 273 election to treat closely related corporations as a single person for zero-rated intercompany app-store and IP-licensing transactions; (ii) ETA section 156 zero-rated intercompany supply election (Form GST25); (iii) tax-deferred rollover elections under ITA subsections 85(1)/85(2) and Quebec Form LM-101-V for corporate restructuring and IP transfers; (iv) associated-corporation allocation election under ITA section 256 with Revenu Quebec Form CO-1027; (v) SR&ED proxy-method election for qualifying software development expenditures (ITA section 37(8)); (vi) ETA section 191.1 election to establish specified-person status for streamlined input tax credit recovery. Hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS Action 2 apply but do not alter the mandatory entity-level classification of a Canadian private corporation; the federal government has not enacted US-style check-the-box regulations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at 9.975%, both administered in Quebec by Revenu Quebec. MMORPG in-app purchases constitute taxable supplies of intangible personal property (digital goods); domestic Canadian sales carry the combined 14.975% rate, while exports to non-residents are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST and QST small-supplier threshold): compulsory registration once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration below the threshold is permitted to recover input tax credits on development costs, App Store/Google Play commissions, and cloud infrastructure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls (CTC). Invoice validity is governed by prescribed elements under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec QST rules (supplier legal name, BN, QST number, date, description, GST/QST amounts or tax-included indication) and records must be retained for six years. Revenu Quebec requires electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns for large registrants; CRA and Revenu Quebec are voluntarily adopting the Pan-Canadian PEPPOL/UBL 2.1 e-invoice framework. App Store Connect and Google Play payout statements must be reconciled to the general ledger and jurisdictional sales reports (country, price tier, tax point, platform fee) to substantiate zero-rating and QST/GST collection on Canadian downloads.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act (section 10: intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada; section 23: exported services) and mirrored under Quebec QST rules. For App Store and Google Play sales, the Canadian publisher makes a zero-rated export supply to the non-resident platform operator or foreign purchaser when the digital content is not for use or enjoyment in Canada; domestic Canadian consumer B2C supplies remain taxable and are collected through the storefront. Conditions for validity: (i) the recipient is a non-resident at the time of supply; (ii) the intangible property is used wholly outside Canada based on location-of-use analysis; (iii) the publisher retains territorial app-store sales reports and Apple/Google platform agreements; (iv) no deemed taxable supply arises in Canada under ETA sections 142/143. Since July 1, 2021, foreign platform operators collect and remit Canadian GST/HST and Quebec QST on B2C Canadian downloads, preserving the Canadian publisher's export zero-rating position on its B2B supply to the platform.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA electronic export reporting via Canadian Export Reporting System or B13A form, as applicable; formally waived for pure digital MMORPG deliveries but retained for any physical collector's media shipments)

Bill of Lading or equivalent transport evidence for tangible mixed deliverables; for digital export substitute server-side delivery logs, CDN access records, and App Store Connect/Google Play transaction manifests

Inward Remittance Certificate: bank MT103 SWIFT receipts, App Store/Google Play payout reconciliation statements, or Payment Service Provider (PSP) settlement reports evidencing foreign-currency or platform-net remittances
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess zero-rated export claims within the normal four-year reassessment period (unlimited in cases of fraud or misrepresentation), re-characterize the supply as taxable at GST 5% plus QST 9.975%, claw back input tax credits, and charge arrears interest at the prescribed rate. Civil penalties include the ETA section 280 false-statement or gross-negligence penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 20% of the net tax evaded, the ETA section 285.1 misinformation penalty, and mirroring QST penalties under Quebec law. Income-tax integration may trigger the ITA section 163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated taxable income where export documentation is fabricated; criminal prosecution under ETA section 327 and ITA section 239 applies to willful evasion, and directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/QST under ETA section 323 and Quebec equivalent, with no minimum-capital shield available. The 180-day repatriation benchmark is a prudent treasury control aligned with App Store/Google Play payout cycles (approximately 30-45 days) and CRA foreign-affiliate tracing expectations; no separate federal FX repatriation statute applies to digital service exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada does not maintain a separate foreign exchange administration authority; exchange-control functions are not centralized in the Bank of Canada. Supervisory responsibility for chartered banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while AML/CFT and money-services-business registration are administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Provincial-level consumer and money-transmitter licensing for Quebec is administered by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible without exchange-control permits or prior central-bank approval for either current or capital account transactions. There is no statutory distinction requiring separate authorization for inbound capital injections, dividend remittances, or trade-related payments. Profit repatriation from the Quebec corporation to non-resident shareholders is legally unrestricted, but is subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act at 25%, reduced where an income tax treaty applies; no further corporate or tax approval is required. The operational risk for an MMORPG treasury is settlement currency concentration in USD/CAD, rather than any regulatory convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no export-proceeds surrender law. There is no statutory timeline requiring repatriation of foreign receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to sell export proceeds to an authorized dealer. Export and royalty proceeds may be retained in Canadian dollars or in a foreign-denominated bank account. Digital game publishing proceeds paid by Apple App Store and Google Play do not trigger customs export declaration requirements; however, receipts above CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC record-keeping and large-transaction reporting by the financial institution, and underlying business contracts should support the commercial nature of the funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Foreign fintech EMIs and cross-border payment platforms can serve as settlement-acceptance and treasury-optimization rails, but they cannot legally replace a Schedule I Canadian bank account for the Quebec corporation. A non-resident electronic-money institution seeking to provide money-transfer or payment services to Canadian clients must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, where applicable, obtain Quebec AMF licensing as a money transmitter. These institutions are not banks, do not hold Canadian banking charters, and cannot provide CDIC-insured deposits or loan facilities. Digital payment providers such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex are best used as supplementary inbound settlement wallets, with scheduled sweeps into the primary operational account at a Canadian chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically at a Quebec branch or head office before account opening. FINTRAC permits non-face-to-face customer identification where the bank follows a reliable, independent document-based verification procedure. In practice, Schedule I banks generally permit remote online onboarding for Canadian-controlled business corporations, including video verification of directors, submission of notarized corporate documents, and electronic signature. For entities with foreign resident directors, opaque offshore structures, or high-risk ownership jurisdictions, bank compliance may impose an enhanced due-diligence interview by telephone or video conference, and in exceptional cases may require an in-person meeting at the bank's commercial banking centre or with a Canadian notary/certified true-copy agent. The remote route is viable for a standard ISIC 5820 digital publisher with transparent Quebec ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of transparent beneficial ownership disclosure on the first account application.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation; federal/Quebec corporate registry extract; articles of incorporation and amendments; updated annual registry declaration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; completed FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership schedule showing all ultimates with 25% or more control; sworn CST/faith declaration; current corporate minute book and shareholder register; directors' identification documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign investors or shareholders resident in a jurisdiction flagged by the bank's sanctions or tax-haven screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds file including audited or reviewed financial statements, personal and corporate bank statements, investment subscription agreements, share-purchase wire confirmations, professional background checks, chain-of-title documents, FATF-country risk explanation, and a legal opinion from the corporate solicitor confirming the investor's identity and legitimacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High anticipated settlement volumes from Apple/Google with no physical inventory and a newly formed entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform agreements for Apple App Store and Google Play; projected revenue dashboard; historical platform payout statements if any; GST/HST/QST registration numbers; prior tax returns where available; payroll to employee records; office lease or remote-work policy; detailed explanation of the IAP business model and a cash-flow treasury plan, including expected FX exposures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Board member or ultimate shareholder identified as a politically exposed person (PEP) or a close associate of a PEP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP assessment; detailed source-of-wealth declaration; enhanced-monitoring and transaction-limit undertaking; board resolution authorizing the officer; senior compliance approval memo; legal opinion confirming no conflict with sanctions lists; ongoing periodic re-certification commitment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate request for international wires and cross-border FX hedging in the first 90 days after incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts, purchase orders and pro-forma invoices for trade disbursements; licensor agreements; employee offer letters and vendor payment schedule; corporate treasury policy delegating FX authority; expected counterparty and country list; FI client-risk-assessment questionnaire; all underlying invoices matching beneficial ownership records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control approval, registration, or purpose-code declaration is required in Canada for inbound equity capital. The recommended compliant route is a SWIFT MT103 international wire from the shareholder's foreign bank to the corporation's CAD or USD operational account at a Schedule I Canadian bank, using the Canadian bank's institution number, transit/branch number, and SWIFT/BIC, with an intermediary correspondent if required. The remittance instruction should identify the ultimate beneficiary legal name, the share-capital purpose in SWIFT field 70, and reference the shareholder resolution. Canadian banks will conduct source-of-funds verification and apply FINTRAC large-transaction reporting where the amount is CAD 10,000 or more. If the bank system requests a purpose standard, the documentation should state equity injection/share subscription; there is no official Canadian 'purpose code' regime. The funds may be received in USD and converted at the bank's commercial FX rate or placed in a non-resident-source USD sub-account pending conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are legally unrestricted and may be executed through SWIFT MT103 international payment orders for ordinary vendor payments and royalty/license settlements. High-value Canadian-dollar domestic payments clear through Lynx (Canada's high-value payment system, successor to LVTS), while lower-value Canadian payments clear through ACSS/Electronic Funds Transfer. USD payments to the United States use Fedwire/CHIPS through the Canadian bank's US correspondent. For commercial trade settlements and larger licensing agreements, a documentary letter of credit issued by the Canadian bank under UCP600 is permissible, as are standby letters of credit under ISP98. The corporation should maintain one master operational account for all treasury inflows and outflows, with pre-authorized settlement instructions to Apple and Google, and should ensure all invoices carry the corporation's GST/HST and Québec QST registration numbers. No official Canadian authorization is required for outbound settlement; banks screen transactions against Canadian and adopted international sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with Schedule I banks under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions
FX swaps for daily liquidity and settlement-date mismatches
Cross-currency swaps for structural balance-sheet hedging of multi-currency receivables
Vanilla FX options, collars, and option combinations with authorized Canadian derivative dealers

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the underlying counterparty jurisdiction imposes convertibility or transferability restrictions; NDFs are not a standard instrument for the freely convertible CAD/USD market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence liability up to CAD 5,000; the Director may administratively dissolve the corporation after notice when two consecutive annual returns are overdue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties apply under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; persistent default can lead to suspension of legal publicity and administrative strike-off from the enterprise register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default up to 12 months; administrative interest accrues on unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CO-17)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default up to 12 months; interest applies under Quebec taxation statutes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No monetary threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a non-distributing private corporation under the CBCA or QBCA; shareholders holding at least 5% of outstanding voting shares may require an audit, and a public reporting issuer must file audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS required for reporting issuers; private enterprises may elect ASPE or IFRS for annual financial reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The federal annual return and Quebec annual declaration serve as the annual confirmation of registered office, directors, and significant-control information; share transfers and control changes must be recorded in the statutory registers before filing, and federal law requires updates to the Register of Individuals with Significant Control within 15 days of any change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

stage_6.entry_description: Net income (loss) before adjustments — tax-basis income reconciled from accounting net income.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: report only income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment (PE); allocate under the applicable treaty (e.g., Art. VII of the Canada-US treaty).
